commentary_segments.text: How to realize a capacitance that can be varied by means of a voltage or current? The Miller effect could be used. An alternative is the circuit in this slide. A differentiator with components R and C is inserted in a d d feedback loop with a variable G block. The input m admittance is easily calculated. It is capacitance C , d multiplied by G R . This m d factor is about 25 in this example. With 4 pF for C , d this allows a capacitance change DC of about 100 pF. If G can now be made positive and negative, then we have a capacitance which is positive m and negative. Current I will be used to control the transconductance G from positive, through zero to 2 m negative values.
